title: Deck detail: edit a deck entry's resolved printing post-import
description: D13 (2026-07-03): decks often run nicer printings for theme/showoff, and the cheapest-first fidelity default plus the cheapest-finish-first reservation rule can misattribute which copies are idle. The deck detail screen should let the user change an entry's resolved printing (and finish, once finish-aware) after import. This is the correction path for D13's accepted tension. Scheduled into Phase 4.

title: Search sort is page-local (sorts only the fetched 100)
description: SearchNotifier sorts results in memory after fetching a page of 100, so e.g. Price high-low on a >100-card result set sorts an arbitrary first page rather than the true top of the full match set. Fix: add ORDER BY support to QueryEngine.search (needed anyway for Phase 4 overflow ranking and deterministic allocation) and rewire the search sort to it. Scheduled into Phase 4 Package 0.

title: AppliedFilterChips crashes on empty-value tokens (t:, r:, is:)
description: PR #2 review comment 3510439797: _chipLabel indexes [0] on the value of t:/r:/is: tokens; an empty value (user submits a bare prefix like t:) throws RangeError during widget build since chips render the raw query before parse validation. Guard with a safe capitalize helper.
close_reason: Added safe _capitalize helper; t:/r:/is: branches no longer index empty values; bare is: shows raw token; regression test added; 313 tests pass

title: have:/unused: placeholders match everything instead of nothing
description: Pre-Phase-3 placeholders compiled have:/unused: to Constant(true), so toggling In collection / Idle only showed all cards despite no collection imports existing. Empty-collection semantics: nothing is owned and nothing is idle, so both should compile to Constant(false) until the Phase 3 user DB replaces them with real subqueries.
close_reason: Placeholders flipped to Constant(false); compiler tests updated (unused:true/have:true empty, -have:true matches all); handoff doc integration notes updated; 312 tests pass

title: Filter panel: multi-rarity OR-grouping and multi-set input
description: Filter panel emitted r:x r:y for multiple rarity selections, which AND together and always return zero results; rarities must OR-group like types. The set field only accepted a single code even though the grammar supports comma lists (s:khm,neo); comma/space-separated input should normalize to one comma list. Includes parse-back (grouped rarities, comma set lists) and applied-chip labels for both.
close_reason: Rarities now OR-group like types ((r:rare OR r:mythic)); set field normalizes comma/space-separated codes to s:a,b,c; parse-back and chip labels updated; 5 new widget tests + chips test file; 310 tests pass

title: Handle multi-face card data (colors/images live in card_faces)
description: Scryfall stores colors and image_uris on card_faces for transform/modal DFC layouts, not at the top level. Currently DFCs like 'Ajani, Nacatl Pariah' show as colorless in c: searches and render without images in the grid. Parser should merge card_faces[0] data (or union colors across faces) during import. Found during Phase 2 browser verification.
close_reason: DFC colors unioned across faces, image_uris from face 0, mana_cost/oracle_text joined from faces; 6 new parser tests; corpus re-import needed to backfill

close_reason: Implemented on phase-2 branch commit a8d61cf

title: Add debug corpus mode for faster dev/test iteration
description: The full Scryfall Default Cards download is ~150MB and takes 1-2 minutes to import on web. For development and testing, add a way to import a smaller corpus instead. Options: (1) use Scryfall's oracle_cards bulk data (~15MB, one printing per card) via a compile-time flag or Settings toggle, (2) provide a pre-built small fixture JSON with ~1000 cards. The debug mode should be opt-in and clearly labeled so users don't accidentally use it in production. Consider a --dart-define=DEBUG_CORPUS=true flag or a developer toggle in Settings.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0bf7a24 on phase-2 branch

title: Add COOP/COEP headers for OPFS storage backend
description: Drift falls back from OPFS to SharedIndexedDb because the browser is missing dedicatedWorkersInSharedWorkers and sharedArrayBuffers features. These require Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp headers. Need to: (1) add a custom Flutter dev server config or proxy that sets these headers for local dev, (2) update the GitHub Pages deploy workflow to serve these headers, (3) verify drift reports OPFS as the storage implementation after the fix. OPFS is significantly faster for bulk inserts than IndexedDB — this should cut import time substantially.
close_reason: COI service worker implemented in 0bf7a24; needs browser verification that drift picks OPFS after the one-time reload

title: Improve onboarding progress feedback with phase labels and card count
description: The onboarding download progress currently just says 'downloading...' for the entire import, which takes 1-2 minutes. The actual phases are: 1) Resolving download URL, 2) Downloading ~150MB, 3) Parsing JSON + inserting cards into DB. The status text and progress bar should reflect which phase is active, and show a card count during the parse/insert phase (e.g. 'Inserting cards... 45,000 / ~100,000'). This would prevent users from thinking the app is stuck.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0bf7a24 on phase-2 branch
